elements.name: Anchor
elements.desc: A hyperlink wrapping SVG content.

doc.summary: A hyperlink that wraps SVG content.
body: `<a>` is SVG's anchor: wrap any shape, group or text in it and that content becomes a clickable link via `href`. It behaves like an HTML `<a>` — `target`, `download`, `rel` and friends all apply.
Because it is a container, the link region is exactly the bounding geometry of whatever it contains.
tips: Add a `<title>` child for an accessible link name and hover tooltip.

elements.name: Animate
elements.desc: Declarative animation — tween an attribute over time.

doc.summary: Declarative SMIL animation — tweens a single attribute over time.
body: `<animate>` smoothly changes one attribute (named by `attributeName`) of its parent element from `from` to `to` (or across a `values` list) over `dur`. `begin`, `repeatCount`, `fill` and `calcMode` control timing, looping and easing.
It runs without any script, defined entirely in markup, making simple motion self-contained inside the SVG.
tips: `fill="freeze"` holds the final value after the animation ends instead of snapping back.
Use `keyTimes`+`keySplines` with `calcMode="spline"` for custom easing curves.

elements.name: Animate motion
elements.desc: Animate an element along a motion path.

doc.summary: Moves an element along a motion path.
body: `<animateMotion>` translates its parent along a trajectory — given inline as a `path`, or by referencing a real `<path>` through a child `<mpath>`. `rotate="auto"` turns the element to face its direction of travel, so it banks through curves.
`keyPoints` with `keyTimes` lets you vary speed along the path rather than moving at constant rate.
tips: Pair it with `<mpath href="#track">` to reuse an existing path as the route.

doc.summary: Animates a transform — translate, scale, rotate or skew.

elements.name: Circle
elements.desc: A perfect circle defined by a centre point and radius.

doc.summary: A circle defined by a centre point and a single radius.
body: `<circle>` is the simplest curved primitive: `cx`/`cy` place the centre and `r` sets the radius. There is no separate width and height — for an oval use `<ellipse>` instead.
A circle with `r="0"` is not rendered. The geometry is exact, so it scales crisply at any zoom.
tips: Stroke straddles the edge — half its width sits outside the radius, half inside.

elements.name: Clip path
elements.desc: Clips an element to an arbitrary shape — hard, 1-bit edges.

doc.summary: Clips an element to an arbitrary shape with hard, 1-bit edges.
body: `<clipPath>` defines a region — built from shapes, paths or text — and everything outside it is cut away when applied via `clip-path="url(#id)"`. Clipping is binary: a pixel is either fully kept or fully removed, giving crisp silhouette edges.
`clipPathUnits` chooses between bounding-box fractions and user-space coordinates for the clip geometry.
tips: For soft, graduated edges or partial transparency use `<mask>` instead — clipping cannot feather.

elements.name: Definitions
elements.desc: Holds reusable definitions that render only when referenced.

doc.summary: A container for reusable definitions that are not drawn until referenced.
body: `<defs>` holds elements that exist to be referenced elsewhere — gradients, patterns, filters, clip paths, markers, symbols and reusable shapes. Nothing inside `<defs>` renders on its own; it becomes visible only when something points at it by `id`, e.g. `fill="url(#grad)"` or `<use href="#icon">`.
Grouping definitions in `<defs>` keeps a document tidy and makes intent explicit, though technically any element with an `id` can be referenced from anywhere.
tips: In this lab the `<defs>` holds a shape with `id="slot"` that a `<use>` instantiates — swap the definition and the rendered shape changes.

elements.name: Description
elements.desc: A long-form accessible description of its parent element.

doc.summary: A long-form, accessible description of its parent element.
body: `<desc>` provides extended descriptive text for the element that contains it, read by assistive technology. It is never rendered visually — its job is semantic, conveying detail that the artwork alone cannot.
Place it as the first child of any container or shape you want to describe; pair it with `<title>` for a short name plus a fuller explanation.
tips: Reference it from the parent with `aria-describedby` for the most reliable screen-reader support.

elements.name: Discard
elements.desc: Removes its target element at a set time.

doc.summary: Removes its target element from the document at a set time.
body: `<discard>` deletes its target (the parent, or an `href` element) once its `begin` time is reached, permanently removing it from the DOM. It is a performance hint for long or looping animations — drop elements that will never be seen again to free resources.
tips: The removal is one-way; the element does not come back.

elements.desc: A circle with independent horizontal and vertical radii.

doc.summary: An ellipse with independent horizontal and vertical radii.
body: `<ellipse>` extends the circle with two radii: `rx` along x and `ry` along y, centred at `cx`/`cy`. Equal radii give a circle.
In SVG 2 `rx` or `ry` may be `auto`, in which case the other radius is used for both — handy when only one axis is known.

elements.name: Blend
elements.desc: Blends two inputs with a Photoshop-style blend mode.

doc.summary: Blends two filter inputs with a Photoshop-style blend mode.
body: `<feBlend>` combines its `in` and `in2` inputs using a `mode` such as `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `darken`, `lighten`, `overlay` or `color-dodge`. The modes match those in image editors, mixing the two layers' colours rather than simply stacking them.
tips: Blend modes only differ visibly when the two layers overlap and contrast — feed it distinct, overlapping inputs.

elements.name: Color matrix
elements.desc: Transforms colours through a matrix — saturate, hue-rotate, recolour.

doc.summary: Transforms colours through a matrix — saturate, hue-rotate or fully recolour.
body: `<feColorMatrix>` multiplies each pixel's [R,G,B,A] by a transformation. `type="matrix"` takes a full 20-value 5×4 matrix for arbitrary channel mixing; `saturate` takes one number (0 = greyscale, 1 = normal); `hueRotate` takes an angle in degrees; and `luminanceToAlpha` turns brightness into opacity.
It is the go-to primitive for tinting, desaturating, channel swaps and converting a graphic into an alpha matte.
tips: `luminanceToAlpha` is a quick way to build a mask from any artwork's brightness.

elements.name: Component transfer
elements.desc: Remaps each colour channel through a transfer function.

doc.summary: Remaps each colour channel through its own transfer function.
body: `<feComponentTransfer>` adjusts colour curves per channel using up to four children — `<feFuncR>`, `<feFuncG>`, `<feFuncB>`, `<feFuncA>`. Each function reshapes its channel: `identity` leaves it, `linear` applies slope+intercept, `gamma` applies amplitude·Cᵉˣᵖ+offset, and `table`/`discrete` remap through a lookup list.
Together they cover brightness, contrast, colour balance, posterisation and thresholding.
tips: `discrete` with a few `tableValues` posterises a channel into hard steps.

elements.name: Composite
elements.desc: Combines two inputs with Porter-Duff or arithmetic compositing.

doc.summary: Combines two inputs with Porter-Duff or arithmetic compositing.
body: `<feComposite>` merges `in` and `in2` using an `operator`: the Porter-Duff set `over`, `in`, `out`, `atop` and `xor` controls how the two layers' coverage combines, while `lighter` adds them.
`operator="arithmetic"` instead computes `result = k1·i1·i2 + k2·i1 + k3·i2 + k4` per channel, a flexible formula for masking, fades and custom mixes via the `k1`–`k4` coefficients.
tips: `operator="in"` is a common way to clip one filter result to the shape of another.

elements.name: Convolve matrix
elements.desc: Convolves pixels with a kernel — blur, sharpen, emboss, edges.

doc.summary: Convolves pixels with a kernel — blur, sharpen, emboss or detect edges.
body: `<feConvolveMatrix>` recomputes each pixel as a weighted blend of its neighbours. `order` sets the kernel size and `kernelMatrix` its weights; `divisor` normalises the result and `bias` offsets it. The chosen weights determine the effect — a centre-heavy kernel sharpens, a ring detects edges, an asymmetric one embosses.
`edgeMode` decides how pixels at the boundary are sampled (`duplicate`, `wrap` or `none`).
tips: It needs textured input to show anything — a flat fill convolves to the same flat colour.

elements.name: Diffuse lighting
elements.desc: Lights an alpha bump-map with matte (diffuse) shading.

doc.summary: Lights an alpha bump-map with matte (Lambertian) shading.
body: `<feDiffuseLighting>` treats its input's alpha channel as a height-field and shades it as a non-shiny surface lit by a child light source (`<feDistantLight>`, `<fePointLight>` or `<feSpotLight>`). `surfaceScale` exaggerates the relief, `diffuseConstant` scales brightness and `lighting-color` tints the light.
The output is opaque RGBA, usually composited back over the original artwork to add dimensional shading.
tips: Blur the alpha source first (`feGaussianBlur` on `SourceAlpha`) so there's a smooth gradient for the light to grade across.

elements.name: Displacement map
elements.desc: Warps one input using another input's pixel values.

doc.summary: Warps one input using the pixel values of another.
body: `<feDisplacementMap>` shifts each pixel of `in` by an amount read from `in2`: `P'(x,y) = P(x + scale·(Xc−0.5), y + scale·(Yc−0.5))`. `xChannelSelector` and `yChannelSelector` pick which channels of the map drive horizontal and vertical displacement, and `scale` sets the strength.
Paired with `feTurbulence` as the map it produces ripples, liquid distortion and organic wobble.
tips: Animate `scale` from 0 for a melt/ripple-in effect.

elements.base:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <defs>
    <filter id="slot" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="130%" height="130%">
      <feTurbulence type="turbulence" baseFrequency="0.05" numOctaves="2" seed="1" result="noiseMap"/>
      <feDisplacementMap data-lab="" in="SourceGraphic" in2="noiseMap" scale="20"></feDisplacementMap>
    </filter>
  </defs>
  <rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#f5a623" filter="url(#slot)"/>
</svg>

elements.name: Distant light
elements.desc: An infinitely-distant directional light for a lighting filter.

doc.summary: An infinitely-distant directional light for a lighting filter.
body: `<feDistantLight>` is a light source used inside `<feDiffuseLighting>` or `<feSpecularLighting>`. Because it is infinitely far away, only its direction matters: `azimuth` is the compass angle in the xy-plane and `elevation` the angle above the surface, like sunlight.

elements.name: Drop shadow
elements.desc: Offset, blurred drop shadow with its own colour.

doc.summary: A one-shot offset, blurred, coloured drop shadow.
body: `<feDropShadow>` is a convenience primitive bundling offset, blur and composite into one step: it blurs the source alpha by `stdDeviation`, offsets it by `dx`/`dy`, tints it with `flood-color`/`flood-opacity`, and draws the original on top.
It replaces the classic `feGaussianBlur`+`feOffset`+`feMerge` recipe with a single, readable element.
tips: Give the `<filter>` room (negative `x`/`y`, >100% width/height) or the shadow clips at the edge.

elements.name: Flood
elements.desc: Fills the filter region with a solid colour.

doc.summary: Fills the entire filter region with a solid colour.
body: `<feFlood>` paints a flat rectangle of `flood-color` at `flood-opacity` across the filter region (or a sub-region you set). On its own it is just a colour block; combined with `feComposite`/`feMerge` it becomes the colour layer behind shadows, tints and glows.

  <defs>
    <filter id="slot"><feFlood data-lab="" flood-color="#e94560"></feFlood></filter>
  </defs>
  <rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#f5a623" filter="url(#slot)"/>
</svg>

elements.name: Gaussian blur
elements.desc: Softens an input by a standard deviation.

doc.summary: Softens an input with a Gaussian blur of a given standard deviation.
body: `<feGaussianBlur>` is the workhorse softening primitive. `stdDeviation` sets the blur amount, and a two-number value blurs x and y by different amounts for directional softness.
Beyond plain blurring it is the first step of most shadows, glows and lighting bump-maps (blurring `SourceAlpha` into a smooth height-field).
tips: `stdDeviation="0"` is a no-op; larger values spread further and need a roomier filter region.

elements.base: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><filter id="slot"><feGaussianBlur data-lab="" stdDeviation="3"></feGaussianBlur></filter></defs><rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#16c79a" filter="url(#slot)"/></svg>

presets.name: edgeMode=none
presets.meaning: none handling at the filter edges

elements.name: Image
elements.desc: Loads an external image or element as a filter input.

doc.summary: Loads an external image or document element as a filter input.
body: `<feImage>` brings outside pixels into the filter chain — referenced by `href` (a raster, an SVG, or even another element by fragment) — so they can be blended, displaced or composited with the source. `preserveAspectRatio` controls how the image fits the region.
tips: Use it to supply a custom texture as the displacement map for `feDisplacementMap`.

elements.base:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <defs>
    <filter id="slot"><feImage data-lab="" href="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSI4MCIgaGVpZ2h0PSI4MCI+PHJlY3Qgd2lkdGg9IjgwIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgwIiBmaWxsPSIjMjIyIi8+PGNpcmNsZSBjeD0iNDAiIGN5PSI0MCIgcj0iMzAiIGZpbGw9IiMxNmM3OWEiLz48L3N2Zz4="></feImage></filter>
  </defs>
  <rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#f5a623" filter="url(#slot)"/>
</svg>

elements.name: Merge
elements.desc: Stacks several filter results into one layered output.

doc.summary: Stacks several filter results into one layered output.
body: `<feMerge>` composites multiple earlier results on top of one another in order, each named by an `<feMergeNode in="...">` child. It is how the shadow recipe puts the blurred, offset shadow underneath the crisp original in a single step.

elements.base:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <defs>
    <filter id="slot">
      <feFlood flood-color="#e94560" x="0" y="0" width="60%" height="60%" result="layerA"/>
      <feFlood flood-color="#4d8bff" x="40%" y="40%" width="60%" height="60%" result="layerB"/>
      <feMerge data-lab=""><feMergeNode in="layerA"></feMergeNode><feMergeNode in="layerB"></feMergeNode></feMerge>
    </filter>
  </defs>
  <rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#f5a623" filter="url(#slot)"/>
</svg>

elements.name: Merge node
elements.desc: One input layer inside an feMerge.

doc.summary: One input layer inside an feMerge.
body: `<feMergeNode>` names a single layer to stack inside its parent `<feMerge>`. Its only attribute, `in`, points at a previous primitive's `result` (or a source keyword); the order of the nodes is the painting order, bottom to top.

elements.base:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <defs>
    <filter id="slot">
      <feFlood flood-color="#f5a623" x="0" y="0" width="70%" height="70%" result="layerA"/>
      <feFlood flood-color="#4d8bff" x="30%" y="30%" width="70%" height="70%" result="layerB"/>
      <feMerge>
        <feMergeNode data-lab="" in="layerA"></feMergeNode>
      </feMerge>
    </filter>
  </defs>
  <rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#e94560" filter="url(#slot)"/>
</svg>

elements.name: Morphology
elements.desc: Fattens (dilate) or thins (erode) an input.

doc.summary: Fattens (dilate) or thins (erode) an input.
body: `<feMorphology>` grows or shrinks the opaque parts of its input. `operator="dilate"` spreads them outward (thicker strokes, bolder text); `operator="erode"` pulls them inward (thinner, eaten away). `radius` sets how far, and a two-number radius works on x and y separately.
tips: Dilate then subtract the original to build an outline/stroke around arbitrary artwork.

elements.base:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <defs>
    <filter id="slot"><feMorphology data-lab="" operator="dilate" radius="3"></feMorphology></filter>
  </defs>
  <text x="50" y="60" text-anchor="middle" font-size="40" font-weight="bold" fill="#f5a623" filter="url(#slot)">SVG</text>
</svg>

elements.name: Offset
elements.desc: Shifts an input by dx/dy — the basis of shadows.

doc.summary: Shifts an input by dx/dy — the foundation of drop shadows.
body: `<feOffset>` simply translates its input by `dx`/`dy` within the filter region. Alone it just moves pixels; offsetting a blurred `SourceAlpha` and merging the original on top is the classic drop-shadow construction.

elements.base:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
  <defs>
    <filter id="slot" x="-20%" y="-20%" width="150%" height="150%"><feOffset data-lab="" dx="4" dy="4"></feOffset></filter>
  </defs>
  <rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#f5a623" filter="url(#slot)"/>
</svg>

elements.name: Point light
elements.desc: A point light source at x/y/z for a lighting filter.

doc.summary: A point light source at a 3-D position for a lighting filter.
body: `<fePointLight>` is an omnidirectional light placed at (`x`,`y`,`z`) inside `<feDiffuseLighting>` or `<feSpecularLighting>`. Like a bare bulb it radiates in all directions, so its position relative to the surface — especially the `z` height — controls where highlights fall and how they spread.

elements.base: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><filter id="slot"><feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6" result="bumpMap"/><feDiffuseLighting in="bumpMap" surfaceScale="5" diffuseConstant="1" lighting-color="#ffffff"><fePointLight data-lab="" x="50" y="50" z="50"></fePointLight></feDiffuseLighting></filter></defs><rect x="20" y="20" width="60" height="60" fill="#ffffff" filter="url(#slot)"/></svg>

elements.name: Specular lighting
elements.desc: Lights an alpha bump-map with glossy (specular) highlights.

doc.summary: Lights an alpha bump-map with glossy specular highlights.
body: `<feSpecularLighting>` is the shiny counterpart to `feDiffuseLighting`: it adds bright, view-dependent highlights to an alpha height-field. `specularConstant` scales highlight intensity and `specularExponent` their tightness (higher = sharper, glassier), while `surfaceScale` and `lighting-color` behave as in diffuse lighting.
Its result is typically composited additively over the artwork to give a wet or metallic sheen.

elements.base: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><filter id="slot"><feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6" result="bumpMap"/><feSpecularLighting data-lab="" in="bumpMap" surfaceScale="5" specularConstant="1" specularExponent="20" lighting-color="#ffffff"><feDistantLight azimuth="45" elevation="45"></feDistantLight></feSpecularLighting></filter></defs><rect x="20" y="20" width="60" height="60" fill="#ffffff" filter="url(#slot)"/></svg>

elements.name: Spot light
elements.desc: A cone-shaped spotlight for a lighting filter.

doc.summary: A cone-shaped spotlight for a lighting filter.
body: `<feSpotLight>` is positioned at (`x`,`y`,`z`) and aimed at (`pointsAtX`,`pointsAtY`,`pointsAtZ`), casting a directional cone of light. `specularExponent` concentrates the beam toward its axis and `limitingConeAngle` clips it to a hard-edged circle of light.

elements.base: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><filter id="slot"><feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6" result="bumpMap"/><feDiffuseLighting in="bumpMap" surfaceScale="5" diffuseConstant="1" lighting-color="#ffffff"><feSpotLight data-lab="" x="70" y="70" z="10" pointsAtX="20" pointsAtY="20" pointsAtZ="0" specularExponent="8" limitingConeAngle="25"></feSpotLight></feDiffuseLighting></filter></defs><rect x="20" y="20" width="60" height="60" fill="#ffffff" filter="url(#slot)"/></svg>

elements.name: Tile
elements.desc: Tiles a filter result across the filter region.

doc.summary: Tiles a filter result repeatedly across the filter region.
body: `<feTile>` takes a small input result (defined by its sub-region) and repeats it edge-to-edge to fill the area. Combined with `feFlood` or `feImage` it builds repeating textures and step-and-repeat patterns entirely within the filter chain.
tips: The tiled input must itself be non-uniform — tiling a flat colour produces the same flat colour.

elements.base: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><pattern id="tilehost" width="25" height="25" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"><rect width="25" height="25" fill="#16c79a"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="6" fill="#f5a623"/></pattern><filter id="slot" x="0" y="0" width="100%" height="100%"><feFlood flood-color="#16c79a" x="0" y="0" width="25" height="25" result="base"/><feFlood flood-color="#f5a623" x="0" y="0" width="13" height="13" result="dot"/><feComposite in="dot" in2="base" operator="over" x="0" y="0" width="25" height="25" result="patch"/><feTile data-lab="" in="patch"></feTile></filter></defs><rect x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" fill="url(#tilehost)" filter="url(#slot)"/></svg>

elements.name: Turbulence
elements.desc: Generates Perlin noise — clouds, marble, organic texture.

doc.summary: Generates Perlin noise — clouds, marble and organic texture.
body: `<feTurbulence>` synthesises procedural noise to fill the filter region. `type="fractalNoise"` gives soft, cloud-like fields; `type="turbulence"` gives sharper, marbled patterns. `baseFrequency` sets the feature scale (small = large blobs), `numOctaves` adds fine detail, and `seed` makes it reproducible.
It is the raw material for textures and, fed into `feDisplacementMap`, for organic distortion.
tips: `stitchTiles="stitch"` makes the noise seamlessly tileable across the region edges.

elements.base: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><filter id="slot" x="-20%" y="-20%" width="140%" height="140%"><feTurbulence data-lab="" type="turbulence" baseFrequency="0.06" numOctaves="3" seed="5"></feTurbulence></filter></defs><rect x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" fill="#4d8bff" filter="url(#slot)"/></svg>

presets.name: seed=5
presets.meaning: random seed 5 for the noise field

elements.name: Filter
elements.desc: A container for a chain of filter primitives.

doc.summary: A container for a pipeline of filter primitives applied as a post-process.
body: `<filter>` holds an ordered chain of `fe*` primitives. Applied via `filter="url(#id)"`, it takes the element's rendering (`SourceGraphic`/`SourceAlpha`) and runs it through the chain to produce effects like blur, shadow, lighting and texture.
`x`/`y`/`width`/`height` define the filter region — the canvas the effect can paint into. Primitives pass results to one another via `result` names and the `in`/`in2` inputs.
tips: Effects often spill outside the element — widen the region (e.g. `x="-20%" width="140%"`) so blurs and shadows aren't clipped.

elements.base: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="120" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><filter data-lab="" id="slot"><feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="3"></feGaussianBlur></filter></defs><rect x="5" y="5" width="90" height="90" fill="#16c79a" filter="url(#slot)"/></svg>

elements.name: Foreign object
elements.desc: Embeds HTML (or other XML) inside SVG.

doc.summary: Embeds HTML (or any other XML namespace) inside an SVG drawing.
body: `<foreignObject>` carves out a rectangular region (`x`,`y`,`width`,`height`) inside the SVG and hands it to another renderer — almost always HTML. It is the bridge for putting wrapping paragraphs, form controls or live web content into a vector scene.
Content must declare its namespace, e.g. a `<div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">`. The region participates in SVG transforms and clipping like any other element.
tips: Support in standalone SVG-as-image contexts is limited — it shines when the SVG is inline in an HTML page.

elements.desc: Arbitrary curves and lines from a `d` command string.

doc.summary: The universal shape — any line or curve from a `d` command string.

doc.summary: The rectangle — SVG's box primitive, positioned by its top-left corner.
body: `<rect>` draws an axis-aligned rectangle. `x`/`y` set the top-left corner and `width`/`height` the size, all in the current user coordinate system. Give `rx`/`ry` a value to round the corners; set only one and the other mirrors it.

doc.summary: The root canvas — and, when nested, a viewport with its own coordinates.
body: `<svg>` is the outermost element of any SVG document, but it can also nest inside another `<svg>` to establish a fresh coordinate system. `viewBox` defines the internal coordinates that map onto the element's `width`/`height`, and `preserveAspectRatio` controls how that mapping fits when the aspect ratios differ.

elements.desc: A reusable template instantiated with its own viewport via `use`.

doc.summary: A reusable template that renders only when instantiated by `<use>`, with its own viewport.
body: `<symbol>` defines graphics meant to be reused, like `<defs>` content, but it is never drawn directly — it appears only through `<use href="#id">`. doc.summary: Stamps a copy of an already-defined element by reference.
body: `<use href="#id">` clones the referenced element (or `<symbol>`) into the document at the `x`/`y` offset you give. The clone is a live, shadow copy: edit the original and every `<use>` of it updates, which is the backbone of icon systems and repeated motifs.
Referencing a `<symbol>` also applies that symbol's own `width`/`height`/`viewBox`, so `<use>` becomes a sized, self-contained instance.
tips: Inherited paint (e.g. `fill`) only reaches the clone for properties the original left unset — set `fill="currentColor"` on the original to recolour per instance.

elements.desc: A named viewport recalled by a URL fragment.

doc.summary: A named viewport you can jump to by URL fragment.
body: `<view id="name">` predefines a `viewBox` (and optional `preserveAspectRatio`) that can be activated by referencing the SVG with that fragment, e.g. `picture.svg#name`. Loading that URL reframes the whole document to the view's box — like a saved camera position.
It renders nothing inline; its only effect is the framing it applies when targeted.
tips: Great for slide-style storytelling or deep-linking to a detail within one SVG file.
